_comment: scripts/install.py writes these for you; this file is for reference or for
clients the installer does not know about.
Replace <YOU> with your Windows user name, and adjust the paths if you
installed the server somewhere other than %LOCALAPPDATA%\3dsmax-mcp.
MCP is a client-side capability: the model behind the client (Claude, GPT,
GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, ...) does not matter, only that the client speaks MCP.
Section A lists stdio (client launches the process).
Section B lists HTTP (cloud/URL-registered clients that cannot).

_deepseek_harness.note: DeepSeek Harness supports both stdio child processes and Streamable HTTP. Use the stdio block above, or the HTTP block in section B.

_why: Cloud-side agents (智谱 BigModel, 阿里云百炼, any web console) cannot spawn
a process on your workstation, so they register an MCP server by URL.
Start the endpoint first and leave it running:

_streamable_http.note: POST /mcp - the current spec. Cursor, Cline, Claude Code all accept this shape.

_with_token.note: When you start with --http-token. Also required if you bind beyond localhost.

_legacy_sse.note: GET /sse + POST /messages - the 2024-11-05 transport. Older Cline builds and several Chinese platforms still speak this.

_reachability: A cloud platform still has to reach your machine. 127.0.0.1 is only visible
locally, so you need port forwarding (frp / ngrok / a reverse proxy) to
publish the endpoint. That exposes control of your 3ds Max scene to whoever
can reach the URL - always combine it with --http-token.

_notes: Every path must be absolute and backslashed. MCP clients do not expand ~ and
do not inherit your shell PATH, which is why PYTHONPATH is set explicitly.
language=auto follows the 3ds Max UI language (ENU -> English, CHS/CHT ->
Chinese). Pin it with "zh" or "en" to stop following.
Smaller --profile values save context: core=119, pipeline=170, animation=178,
